newsitem.title: CANADA: Lawyer continues fight against Quebec secession.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer continues fight against Quebec secession.

text.p: A Quebec lawyer said on Tuesday he was proceeding with his Quebec court bid to block any future referendums that lead to a unilateral declaration of independence by the French-speaking Canadian province.

Lawyer Guy Bertrand told reporters he will also seek to participate in the Canadian government's appeal to the Supreme Court of Canada on the legality of any such unilateral declaration of independence (UDI) by Quebec.
"No one is above the law. The Quebec government must respect the Canadian legal and constitutional framework," Bertrand said.
Bertrand said he wants to argue in the Supreme Court action "on the behalf of the citizens of Quebec whose rights and freedoms are threatened by the unilateral secession of Quebec."
Bertrand, a former staunch separatist turned defender of Canadian unity, will continue his court fight on Oct. 10.

He is asking the Quebec Superior Court to rule on four questions relating to Quebec's right to secede unilaterally after a referendum vote in favour of such action. The federal government is asking the Supreme Court for a similar ruling.

The Quebec government has said that it will not appear in court to defend against either action, arguing that only Quebec voters can decide the province's political future through a democratic referendum.

Bertrand began his court action after Quebec separatists lost a referendum on sovereignty by one percentage point in October 1995. In August, a Quebec judge ruled that his bid to seek an injuction against future sovereignty referendums should be heard in court.
